leads.summary: The provider gear and open PR #11967 each bind the hero's single trailingControl, yielding a QML load error if both merge
leads.consequence: Both PRs are diverged, and GitHub calls #11967 MERGEABLE; git merge-file exits 0 without conflict markers, but the combined PanelHero has trailingControl: Component at lines 749 and 791 of the same object. Qt's QML builder rejects duplicate singular property bindings with 'Property value set multiple times'; the agents widget cannot load, so neither the provider switches nor Go credentials card is reachable. Combine the two controls within one trailingControl binding or give the second one its own container. The existing agents-panel-test.sh still passes this invalid merged source.
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator (triage/pr-11967.diff:328, sol/merged-11967/combined-Panel.qml:749,791 on hero, qqmlirbuilder.cpp:285) and by Opus self-check headless load (opus/plan-draftcheck2/runs/20260928T030732Z-f0e0aff5); published

leads.summary: Switching off a provider identified by its record does not skip its collector if the record id differs from the collector filename
leads.consequence: The new switch writes providers[record.id].enabled=false and updateCommand emits --except <record.id>, but the updater filters by omarchy-agent-usage-<filename suffix>. A collector 'mismatch' returning a valid record with id 'alias' continues running on every normal and limits refresh after 'alias' is switched off, despite the UI/README promise to stop refreshing it. The persisted record stays hidden until the switch is turned on, and the next run still collects it. This affects custom collector ids permitted by the updater today, and also the namespaced 'claude-work' accounts planned in open #10080: that PR calls wanted('claude') before writing each nested claude-* record, so --except claude-work cannot stop the work account collector. Reconcile ids at the updater boundary or clarify that one group cannot selectively skip a nested provider.
leads.triage: dropped: pre-existing updater design; first-party collectors AGENT_ID match filenames (Opus final); only a hypothetical mismatched third-party collector triggers it

leads.summary: Discovered provider ids that are inherited Object keys disappear from the new switch list
leads.consequence: The ordinary object seen={} makes seen['constructor'], seen['toString'], seen['__proto__'] and seen['hasOwnProperty'] already truthy. A valid usage record with any of these ids has its data counted and can make the bar icon visible, but its switch is never generated (even when also present in agentIds or providers). If it is configured off by hand, the panel may open directly into settings with no row to re-enable it. Use Object.create(null) or a Set with explicit ownership checks for id deduplication.
leads.triage: dropped: contrived ids with no real collector; low value for public comment

leads.summary: The existing agents-panel fixture does not assert any switch-view behavior

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** in a headless check of the head against the merge-base, the provider switches behave as the PR body describes. Four smaller points follow: a stale view after switching a provider back on, an inaccurate startup-gate comment, an overlap with open PR #11967, and a pre-existing writer limitation that the switches now expose.

| Scenario (synthetic records and settings) | Observed at head |
|---|---|
| Flip `claude` off with `providers: {claude: {enabled: true, note: "hand"}, zeta: {enabled: false}}` | Writes `claude: {enabled: false, note: "hand"}`, keeps `zeta`; update command gets `--except claude --except zeta` |
| Same flip repeated | No writer call, no notification |
| Writer returns `false`, or no writer | Previous `settings` restored; one `'omarchy-notification-send' 'Couldn'\''t save provider settings' 'The switch was put back.'` |
| Every provider with data switched off | Bar icon stays visible (base: hidden); panel opens on the switches at row 0 |
| `j`/`k`, Enter, `s`, Esc (simulated through the key catcher's signals) | `j`/`k` clamp to the list, Enter flips the highlighted row, `s` opens the view at row 0; Esc returns to the dashboard, or closes the panel when everything is off |
| Only an all-zero leftover record | Icon stays hidden, with or without a `providers` map |

From source review, the dashboard keys, provider switching and IPC paths are unchanged outside the switch view; of those, only Enter-to-refresh on the dashboard was exercised.

### Switching a provider back on shows its old numbers until the next refresh

`setProviderEnabled` (and the Toggle and Enter paths that call it) never triggers a collection. While a provider is off, the updater skips it, but its old `<id>.json` record stays in the usage directory. Switching it back on makes `enabledProviders` show that record immediately, so the hero, limits, "Tokens by day" and model rows can show figures from whenever it was switched off.

**Impact:** stale usage is displayed as current until the next refresh: a manual one (`r`, or Enter on the dashboard), or the next scheduled one, which is up to `refreshIntervalSec` away (900 s by default). Limits alone also refresh on the next panel open.

**Suggested change:** after a successful enable, run a targeted collection such as `usage.runUpdate("normal", [id])`. `updateCommand` already passes positional ids, and the updater treats them as an allow-list.

### Startup-gate comment does not match Bar.qml

The comment above `settingsReady` in `Main.qml` says `injectProps` delivers `bar`, `moduleName` and `settings` "a tick after it builds the widget". In `shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml` the Loader's `onLoaded` calls `slot.injectProps()` synchronously, then again through `Qt.callLater`. `Timer.triggeredOnStart` fires from a posted event (`QQmlTimerPrivate::maybeTick()`), so on the built-in bar the pre-PR first refresh should already see the injected settings. A harness that mirrors Bar.qml's injection order confirmed this; the real bar was not loaded.

```text
First refresh, synthetic host with `codex` switched off (headless, single run)
host injection            base                     head
sync in onLoaded (bar)    --except codex           --except codex
one tick later            no --except (scrapes)    --except codex
no bar at all             --except codex           --except codex after ~6 s
```

**Impact:** the gate is correct and does help hosts that inject a tick later. On the default bar it should change nothing (no path where it does was found), and a host without a bar now waits about 6 s for its first collection. The comment will mislead anyone maintaining the gate.

**Suggested change:** reword the comment to describe the case the gate actually covers. If a specific host showed the start-up scrape, naming it in the comment would help.

### Overlap with open PR #11967

Open PR #11967 ("Agents: user collectors + Go connection settings card") also adds a gear through `trailingControl` on the same `PanelHero` in `shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml`. A textual three-way merge of the two branches produces no conflict markers, but it leaves two `trailingControl: Component { ... }` bindings on one object. Loading the merged `Panel.qml` headlessly fails with `Panel.qml:791:13: Property value set multiple times`.

**Impact:** if both changes are combined as they stand, the agents panel fails to load, and `agents-panel-test.sh` still passes on that merged source, so it would not catch this.

**Suggested change:** coordinate with #11967 on a single hero control, for example one container holding both gears.

**Optional (pre-existing):** `updateEntryInline` in `shell/shell.qml` matches only object layout entries. A bare string entry such as `"omarchy.agents"`, which is what the rename migration `migrations/1786099804.sh` produces from a string entry, makes every flip return `false`. The PR then reverts correctly and shows "Couldn't save provider settings" with no reason. Promoting a matching string entry to `{id}` in the shared writer would fix this for every inline writer.

**Optional test improvement:** `agents-panel-test.sh` and `qml-text-format-test.sh`, which the PR body cites, pass identically on the merge-base and head. The six assertions in `agents-panel-test.sh` only match the bar button's click wiring, so an empty `setProviderEnabled` would still pass them. A small test for the merge and no-op rules, the `allProvidersOff` visibility rule and the resulting `--except` arguments would catch that.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `ef7ff3e` against merge-base `47de632` and the current `quattro` tip (whose only agents-plugin change, `IpcHandler` to `ShellIpc`, does not interact). Headless Quickshell harness loading the real `Panel.qml` and `Main.qml` with a synthetic bar, synthetic usage records, a stub updater and a stub settings writer. Keyboard input was simulated through the panel key catcher's signals. The keyboard panel window was replaced by a same-API stub, so window placement, focus, rendering, hover styling and scrolling of a long switch list were not exercised. No desktop session and no screenshots. `updateEntryInline` was run extracted from `shell/shell.qml` against three `shell.json` shapes. The #11967 overlap was checked by a textual three-way merge of `Panel.qml` and a headless load of the merged file.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
